root_cause.text: In `netfilter/nft_inner`’s `nft_inner_parse_l2l3()` IPv6 handling, the code wrongly overwrote the transport-header offset returned by `ipv6_find_hdr()` with `nhoff + sizeof(struct ipv6hdr)`, so `ctx->inner_thoff` pointed only past the IPv6 base header instead of after extension headers while `l4proto` remained correct.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the line `thoff = nhoff + sizeof(_ip6h);` from the IPv6 `fragoff == 0` path, and the commit message states that `ipv6_find_hdr()` “correctly computes the transport header offset traversing all extension headers” but its result was “immediately overwritten” by the 40-byte base-header offset, causing `inner_thoff`/`l4proto` desynchronization and potential firewall bypass.

intent_record.intent_summary: Preserve the existing transport-header offset in the IPv6 non-fragment case instead of unconditionally resetting it.
intent_record.what: The assignment `thoff = nhoff + sizeof(_ip6h);` was removed from the `fragoff == 0` branch in `nft_inner_parse_l2l3()`. The surrounding code still sets `ctx->flags |= NFT_PAYLOAD_CTX_INNER_TH;`, `ctx->inner_thoff = thoff;`, and `ctx->l4proto = l4proto;`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code no longer overwrites `thoff` with the IPv6 header end offset when the fragment offset is zero. Instead, it preserves whatever value `thoff` already had, which changes the transport-header offset used by later processing and avoids forcing an IPv6-specific offset in this branch.

grouping_result.intent: Preserve the existing transport-header offset in the IPv6 non-fragment case instead of unconditionally resetting it.

relevance_review.reason: The group’s core intent matches the root cause: it fixes IPv6 inner parsing so the transport-header offset is preserved rather than being reset to the IPv6 base header, which is exactly the bug described.

candidates.rationale: This line unconditionally overwrote the transport-header offset returned by ipv6_find_hdr(), causing ctx->inner_thoff to point only past the IPv6 base header instead of after any extension headers.

vuln_statements.explanation: This assignment overwrote the transport-header offset previously returned by ipv6_find_hdr(), so ctx->inner_thoff was set only to the end of the IPv6 base header rather than after any extension headers, while the protocol value remained correct.

bic_trace_step.reason: The IPv6 path in `nft_inner_parse_l2l3()` is present and shows the problematic logic. It calls `ipv6_find_hdr(pkt->skb, &thoff, -1, &fragoff, &fh_flags);`, but then, even after obtaining the transport offset in `thoff`, it overwrites it with `thoff = nhoff + sizeof(_ip6h);` before storing `ctx->inner_thoff = thoff;` and `ctx->l4proto = l4proto;`. This means `inner_thoff` is forced to point only past the IPv6 base header instead of after extension headers, which matches the reported root cause. There is no corrective handling here to preserve the offset returned by `ipv6_find_hdr()`, so the fix is not present in this commit.
